sentences.text: JUDGMENT 1.

The present claim proceedings have emanated from Detailed Accident Report (hereinafter referred to as DAR) filed on 30.03.2019 with reference to FIR No.414/2019 registered at PS Shalimar Bagh in respect of commission of offences of causing hurt by rash and negligent driving of a motor vehicle on a public road as well as for the commission of offence of mischief by causing damage to private property having value of more than Rs.50/- punishable U/s 279/337/427 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereinafter referred to as IPC) wherein subsequent charge sheet for the commission of offences causing grievous hurt by rash and negligent driving of motor vehicle on a public road as well as for the commission of offence of mischief by causing damage to private property having value of more than Rs.50/- punishable U/s 279/338/427 IPC against driver,
namely, Arun Kumar was also filed in respect of grievous injuries sustained by victim Sh. Khushiram (hereinafter also referred to as the injured/claimant/petitioner) in a road traffic accident.

The learned predecessor Court had vide order dated 30.03.2019 treated the DAR as a petition u/s 166(4)

The brief facts of the case as discernible from the petition/DAR and documents of the petitioner are that on 28.07.2018 at about 10:30 pm, petitioner, a vegetable seller by profession was going from his residence at Pitampura with his handcart (rickshaw rehri) of vegetables and upon reaching near MCD School at Nirman Camp, Haiderpur, one Tata Magic Gramin Sewa Vehicle bearing registration No. DL2W-1699 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) being driven by its driver, namely, Arun Kumar (hereinafter referred to as driver of the offending vehicle/Respondent no.1/R1) at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner had come from behind and had hit his handcart with great force.

As a consequence of being hit by the offending vehicle, his rehri had got badly damaged and had also collided against another handcart of a golgappa seller whereas he himself had fell down on the road and had become unconscious.

It is further the case of the petitioner that the golgappa seller, who was an eye witness of the case accident and whose rehri was also badly damaged in the case accident had made a call to the police at 100 number after which he had been taken to MAX Hospital, Shalimar Bagh, Delhi, where he was medically examined vide MLC No.2683 containing a finding to the effect that he (the petitioner) had sustained grievous injuries in the case accident.

The petitioner was advised admission in hospital to rule out fracture injuries of head and cervical spine as well as fracture injury of right thigh, however, the petitioner could not afford the cost of treatment at MAX Super Speciality Hospital, Shalimar Bagh, Delhi and had left the said hospital against medical advice on 29.07.2018.

sentences.text: 10.3 R1 and R2 had failed to appear in the court despite waiting till 12:30 pm, hence their cross-examination was treated as nil despite being opportunity having being given to them to cross-examine PW1.
10.4 R1/driver of the offending vehicle, R2/owner of the offending vehicle and R3/insurance company had not examined any witness in support of their version of the case.

10.5 No material contradiction or discrepancy had appeared in the cross examination of PW1 to discredit his version narrated in his examination-in- chief recorded by way of affidavit and thus, it has been established that the case accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.
PW1 is the victim who had sustained injuries in the alleged accident.
He seems to be a reliable and truthful witness who has withstood his cross-examination by defence.

10.6 The copy of criminal case record shows that the case FIR No.414/2018 U/s 279/337/427 of Indian Penal Code 1860 (hereinafter referred to as IPC) was registered at Police Station Shalimar Bagh in the present matter wherein subsequently the charge sheet for the commission of offences punishable u/s 279/338/427 IPC was also filed against R1/driver of the offending vehicle.
10.7 The issue no. 1 is only to be proved by claimant beyond preponderance of probabilities as distinguished from beyond reasonable doubt.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, the charge sheet u/s 279/338/427 IPC filed against R1 can also be relied upon to show that the case accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1.

In the said circumstances, from the testimony of Khushi Ram Vs. Arun Kumar & Ors. Page 11 of27 PW1/petitioner and other record including charge sheet filed against R1, it has been clearly proved on the scale of preponderance of probabilities that the case accident had occurred at the above said date, time and place and in the above said manner due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R1 and thereby grievous injuries had been sustained by the petitioner.
Issue no. 1 is accordingly decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
He seems to be a reliable and truthful witness who has withstood his cross-examination by defence.
However, he has not filed any original medical bill on record to establish his expenses on his medical treatment.
As such, there is no document on record to establish the fact that the petitioner had in fact incurred any expenses on his medical treatment or not.
In such circumstances, the expenses, if any, incurred by the petitioner on taking special diet for speedy recovery and conveyance for travel to hospital during his treatment period have to be ascertained on the basis of nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the case accident.
In such circumstances, as such there is no material on record to arrive at a finding to the effect that petitioner had in fact found it necessary to avail or felt compelled to avail services of any medical attendant during his treatment period and had incurred any expenses on the same or not.
Accordingly, no amount is being granted as compensation towards attendant charges to the petitioner under this head.
In fact, there is no material on record to suggest as to which part of body of the petitioner had sustained such injury which might require treatment in future and as such this Tribunal cannot determine the requirement of future treatment faced by the petitioner in the aftermath of the case accident without any medical evidence.
Accordingly, no amount is being granted as compensation towards future medical expenses to the petitioner under this head.
16. Pain and Suffering 16.1
In this context, a perusal of the MLC of the petitioner bearing No.2683 reveals that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the case accident.
Therefore, in the interest of justice, in the present case, this court is of the opinion that the claimant/petitioner is entitled to interest @ 7 % per annum from the date of filing of DAR/petition, that is, with effect from 30.03.2019 till realisation of the compensation amount.

who was the driver of the offending vehicle was not having a valid driving licence conferring authority upon him to drive a motor vehicle on a public road issued in his favour by the competent authority.
Moreover, the insurance policy of the offending vehicle stood valid in favour of R2/Kamal Jain as on the date of the occurrence of the alleged accident.
As per settled law, since the offending vehicle was duly insured with the insurance company/R3, hence R3 is liable to pay the entire compensation amount to the petitioner as per law.
